[b]The Little Box Countdown - Bubba's 13th Auction - small-sized games for the New Year - ends Jan 1 at 9PM ET[/b] These small games are looking for new homes. They are ALL SMALL – and will fit in your backpack, briefcase, suitcase, purse, or maybe even your pocket. Many are HARD-TO-FIND. In Santa’s workshop, you must fulfill a wish list by exchanging, passing, or even stealing cards. Overview You are one of the helpers at Santa’s workshop and have been assigned to fulfill the wishlist of two children by exchanging, passing, or even stealing cards from other players. Be the first to complete both of your assignments and you win!
Components The North Pole contains 18 poker sized cards, that include into two types of cards: Assignment cards (4) and Present Cards (14). Assignment cards show your assigned wishlists, with one on each side. Each wish list has 3 items, Present cards have two parts: the present associated with a wishlist and a power to use during play.
Game Play: Draw cards from the draw or discard pile until you have 2 cards in your hand. Do one of the following: Play a card and resolve its power. Discard a card and draw a card from the draw pile. Pass and take no action. Check for completion of your assignment. If complete do the following: Reveal your present cards If you have the gift card, discard it. Return any remaining cards to your hand.

Struggle for Island Supremacy! Game Market 2017 Spring (Tokyo) Send your tribes to islands numbered 1–12 by rolling dice. The game ends when a player conquers 7 islands, or when someone can no longer send in a tribe (in which case that player is eliminated). Among the remaining players, the one with the most VP from islands wins.
[imageid=9305417 original][imageid=9305421 original]
Rules: Line up 1 to 12 island cards, and each person has 15 tribal cubes. Each player decides to send 3 dice, one as it is, and two add two to the island to send. If it's 2, 3, 4, 4 and 5 or 3 and 6, etc. If no one has settled on the island yet, put a tribe cube. If someone is settled, put that number + 1 cube and drive out the opponent. If you have already settled in, you can adjust the number of cubes between the islands. The exit of the dice can be changed by discarding the cube. The end condition of the game is to conquer 7 islands, or if someone can no longer send a tribe, that person will be eliminated, and the person with the most VPs on the island will win.

You and your partner are in charge of city planning for two towns separated by a river. The goal of the game is to attract more citizens to your town than your opponent’s. A balance of luck and strategy High replayability Tactical mind games with your opponent Easy to learn, but hard to master Just the right play time All of these convey the unique enjoyment that only analog (tabletop) games can provide. Players who enjoy two-player–only games such as Geister, Jaipur, Patchwork, Targi, or Battle Line will also find this game appealing, especially those at an intermediate level or higher. In the new edition (the version shown in the main image: 2019 edition), the core rules remain unchanged, but fine adjustments have been made to various details of gameplay. 🇯🇵 JAPAN ボードゲーム ボスサリーノ(Bossarino) Bossarino, a 2-player hidden boss hide-and-seek board game by Q's Games where one player hides their boss among upside-down hats, and the other tries to find it by moving and challenging pieces. The game involves square grid movement, challenging opponents, and strategic placement of pieces, with a goal of either finding the hidden boss or helping your own boss escape.
Why not take advantage of the Multi-Win discount ? -- pair with The Catfather and another.
Gameplay Overview Players: 2 players Objective: One player hides their "boss" under one of several upside-down hats or pieces, while the other player tries to locate it. Mechanics: Players take turns moving pieces on a square grid. Moves: Move a piece one space in any direction. Swap positions with an opponent's piece. Challenge an opposing piece, which presumably reveals whether it's the boss or not. Winning: The game ends when the hidden boss is found or the player successfully moves their boss off the board, depending on the specific game setup.

Game Overview Send your own crew aboard a spaceship and launch it toward planetary development! Sometimes… aliens sneak on board!? This is a board game full of psychological mind games and area-majority competition. It’s not a straightforward area-control game—card effects can completely throw off your calculations, or trigger unexpected twists that turn everything upside down. If something strange happens in a room, it can become a serious problem! Use cards to construct rooms on the rocket and assign your crew to them carefully. But be warned: rocket food is limited! If you get too greedy and send too many crew members, you could be eliminated. Make smart use of the game’s constraints and outplay your opponents!
Genre: Area Majority For 2 to 4 players. Play time: 30 minutes Recommended Age: 8 years and up. Game Design: Ocavenius
[Set Contents] 1 x Map 31 basic cards 4 x Rocket Tips 4 Boosters 7 Planet Cards 1 x Space Station 4 x Summary 48 crew tiles in 4 colors 1 x Alien Tile 1 x Instruction

Trick or Trick TRICK or TRICK Theme/Flavor: Horror, Modern Mechanics: Worker Placement, Rock–Paper–Scissors system, Chicken Race Game Designer: ASOBOARD! (遊ぼーど！) Publisher - Minori
A worker-placement, musical-chairs rock–paper–scissors game where cute little monsters play pranks on each other! Game Market Autumn 2022 Cute monsters battle by pulling pranks on one another in a party-like theme as they all seek the legendary sweets that everyone falls in love with—the mythical “Jack-o’ Cookies.” In this game, players use the hand icons printed on cards, and at the end of each round they face off in a decisive rock–paper–scissors showdown. In the first half of the round, players take turns placing their monsters onto spaces with pranks (effects), allowing them to look at opponents’ hands, swap cards, and more. Each player works to assemble the hand they need for the rock–paper–scissors battle. However, there are also “pranks that can accidentally knock you out,” so you must maneuver carefully to avoid clogging your hand and being forced to trigger one of these effects. Conversely, bold strategies that outwit and eliminate your opponents are also essential. Among the cute monsters, there is a single, most powerful monster called the Reaper. This monster has an ultimate skill: it defeats every hand in rock–paper–scissors. However, it comes with a restriction—it cannot be played onto the field during the prank phase. Because it takes up space in your hand, it constantly puts you at risk of elimination. If you obtain the Reaper, whether you can secretly carry it into the final rock–paper–scissors showdown without revealing it will bring you much closer to victory. Despite its adorable appearance, this is an intense and thrilling game that demands strategies focused on trapping, deceiving, and outmaneuvering your opponents.
